title: Discover the public and host surfaces
persona: A first-time host checking whether OpenRoom is ready for a live session.
purpose: Walk the public home, documentation, participant join, and signed-out host entry points.
outcome: The visitor can distinguish the participant, stage, and host surfaces before signing in.

chapters.title: Start at the product home
chapters.narration: We begin at the public home. This is the promise surface, so the first question is simple: can a new host understand what happens here and where the live session begins?

actions.name: Hear from everyone, not just the first hand up.

chapters.title: Check the documentation entry point
chapters.narration: Next we open the documentation. A good walkthrough should expose the handoff from product promise to operating instructions, not leave the host to guess which surface is authoritative.

chapters.title: Check the participant entry point
chapters.narration: The participant does not enter through the host workspace. The join route is deliberately separate, and it should make the session code and account-free recovery path obvious.

chapters.title: Inspect signed-out host entry
chapters.narration: Finally we open the host workspace while signed out. This is a useful boundary check: the workspace should explain what requires an account without pretending that the visitor is already authenticated.
